documents.unit: Division of Information Resources & Technology and Office of the Provost
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy (University Policies)
documents.stance_why: The document restricts AI use for university business and data: members 'must not enter Rowan internal, confidential, proprietary or regulated data' into public tools, and business 'must only be processed in officially approved AI/LLM platforms'. It sets no rule for student coursework and defers to the Academic Integrity Policy, so the stance is restrict for the area it governs.
documents.summary: A university-wide Information Security policy on AI and LLMs adopted in 2024 and revised in 2026. It forbids putting non-public Rowan data into public AI tools and confines university business, including academic communication, to approved platforms. It addresses coursework only by deferring to the Academic Integrity Policy.

units.why: The purpose clause sets the policy's scope as 'secure use of AI and Large Language Models' and 'Rowan data of all classification levels'; an institution-level framework statement, so P56, informs.
units.anchor: establish requirements for the secure use of AI and Large Language Models

units.why: States who the policy binds: 'all members of the Rowan Community who access and use the University's electronic information and information systems'. A scope statement, so P61.
units.anchor: applies to all members of the Rowan Community
units.fit_note: Scope is by community membership and system access; no definition of AI is given here (definitions are referred to a separate glossary).

units.why: Assigns implementation to named officers: 'Vice Presidents and Deans shall implement this policy'. Governance of who implements the policy; closest is P56 but it assigns responsibility.
units.anchor: The Vice Presidents and Deans shall implement this policy.
units.fit_note: Assigns who implements the policy rather than stating purpose or principles.

units.why: 'The use of AI tools must adhere to all Rowan University policies' ties AI use to existing university policy, so P77 with 'must'.
units.anchor: The use of AI tools must adhere to all Rowan University policies

units.why: Members must follow HR, legal and ethical requirements 'with regard to data use, privacy, consent, ownership, and academic integrity'; compliance with existing law and policy, so P77.
units.anchor: must adhere to human resource and legal requirements, as well as ethical standards

units.why: Warns that 'AI generated transcripts of meetings may create records subject to OPRA'; a legal-records compliance duty for employees ('should be aware'), P77.
units.anchor: AI generated transcripts of meetings may create records subject to OPRA

units.why: Bans entering sensitive data into public tools: 'must not enter Rowan internal, confidential, proprietary or regulated data ... into publicly-available AI tools'. Data protection, P50 (P20 is about assignments and code, not institutional data).
units.anchor: must not enter Rowan internal, confidential, proprietary or regulated data

units.why: 'must only be processed in officially approved AI/LLM platforms' limits academic, administrative and operational work to vetted tools; P50 (prefer vetted tools), stated as a requirement.
units.anchor: must only be processed in officially approved AI/LLM platforms
units.fit_note: Goes beyond preferring vetted tools: it makes approved platforms mandatory for all university business including academic communications.

units.why: 'This ensures compliance with the University's obligations for data discoverability' gives the legal reason for the approved-platform rule; nearest is P65 (vendor and data-sharing governance).
units.anchor: This ensures compliance with the University's obligations for data discoverability.
units.fit_note: Gives the legal reason (data discoverability) for the approved-platform rule rather than reviewing vendor agreements.

units.why: Purchases of AI services 'must be procured through the standard processes' of IRT and Contracting & Procurement; operational governance of AI acquisition, P76.
units.anchor: must be procured through the standard processes

units.why: Meetings 'may only be recorded by AI platforms that are authorized, secured and managed by IRT': an operational rule on AI recording, P76.
units.anchor: may only be recorded by AI platforms that are authorized

units.why: AI transcription of confidential HR meetings 'should not be used except in circumstances where prior Human Resources permission has been obtained'; administrative AI use rule, P76.
units.anchor: should not be used except in circumstances where prior Human Resources permission

units.why: 'AI requirements related to coursework must comply with the Academic Integrity Policy' sets no coursework rule itself and defers to the existing integrity policy; P77 (comply with existing university policy).
units.anchor: AI requirements related to coursework must comply with the
units.fit_note: Also functions as a deferral: this policy leaves coursework AI rules to the Academic Integrity Policy.

units.why: 'Questions regarding the use of AI ... should be directed to the Rowan University Office of Ethics, Academic Integrity or Research' points people to human offices, P72 (closest).
units.anchor: Questions regarding the use of AI or data mining tools should be directed
units.fit_note: Directs questions to administrative offices rather than to writing centers, librarians or instructors as support alongside AI.

units.why: 'The use of AI may not infringe on copyright laws' is a copyright constraint on AI use, P52, must-not.
units.anchor: may not infringe on copyright laws applicable to U.S. universities
units.frag_start: The use of AI may not

units.why: 'Any individual who violates this policy shall be subject to discipline up to and including dismissal' states the consequence of violation in advance; P37 though penalties are named only as a range and cover employees mainly.
units.anchor: shall be subject to discipline up to and including dismissal from the University
units.fit_note: Penalty is a range up to dismissal, tied to the data-security policy rather than to coursework misconduct.

units.why: 'Any exceptions to this policy must be approved by the Information Security Office and Office of the Provost' creates an exception-approval route; no type fits an exceptions procedure.
units.anchor: Any exceptions to this policy must be approved by the Information Security Office

documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence & Teaching
documents.stance_why: The page says 'The University does not have a universal generative AI policy. Instructors may select one of the following statements', then offers samples from 'No generative AI' to 'Some generative AI' and a generic one. The decision is handed to instructors, with tiers listed, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: The Faculty Center page states that Rowan has no universal generative AI policy and recommends that instructors put a statement in their syllabi and Canvas. It offers four sample statements from no AI to limited AI, advises against AI detectors, and links to many external resources.

units.why: Recommends syllabus statements: 'Faculty should include a clear and specific statement in their syllabi and Canvas'. Requirement to state AI expectations, P09, should.
units.anchor: Faculty should include a clear and specific statement in their syllabi
units.frag_end: may or may not be used in their classes.

units.why: 'The University does not have a universal generative AI policy' states that no single rule exists and the decision lies with instructors; P04.
units.anchor: The University does not have a universal generative AI policy.

units.why: 'Instructors may select one of the following statements if appropriate to their classroom' hands choice to the instructor, P04, may.
units.anchor: Instructors may select one of the following statements

units.why: The heading 'Sample syllabus statements for varying usage of AI in the classroom' introduces a menu of statements from no AI to some AI plus a generic one; named categories of use, P05.
units.anchor: Sample syllabus statements for varying usage of AI in the classroom

units.why: Option 1 says use of ChatGPT and similar tools 'will be considered a violation of academic integrity'; a default ban in the sample statement, P01, student must-not.
units.anchor: will be considered a violation of academic integrity and will be treated accordingly

units.why: Option 1 lists consequences: students 'may fail the assignment, fail the course, or face other sanctions'; concrete penalties in advance, P37.
units.anchor: may fail the assignment, fail the course, or face other sanctions

units.why: 'Violations that result in a grade penalty must be reported to the Provost's Office' is a reporting duty in the integrity process, P36 (nearest).
units.anchor: must be reported to the Provost's Office
units.fit_note: A duty to report graded penalties to the Provost's Office, not the classification of the misconduct.

units.why: 'students should provide appropriate documentation whenever quoting, paraphrasing, summarizing, or otherwise using the language or ideas of others' asks students to acknowledge sources; P24 (documentation of outside material).
units.anchor: students should provide appropriate documentation whenever quoting, paraphrasing, summarizing
units.fit_note: Written about sources generally, not AI specifically.

units.why: Option 2 explains that unauthorized AI 'defeats the purpose, misrepresents your mastery of the material'; rationale that AI shortcuts skill-building, P41, informs.

units.why: Option 3 allows AI 'as a tool to support learning (e.g., in obtaining feedback or generating ideas)'; brainstorming and feedback use, P15 (closest).

units.why: 'work submitted by a student should be that of the student and not the work of an AI system' bars AI-produced submissions, P19, should.

units.why: 'it should be cited like any other reference material' requires citation of AI-generated material, P24.
units.anchor: it should be cited like any other reference material

units.anchor: the student bears responsibility for any inaccuracies or misinformation
